title: Theorems & proofs
blurb: SEE send-up mnemonics and theorem cards: proof moves, exceptions, and exam-style drills for geo + trig.

heron.name: Heron's formula
heron.also: Semi-perimeter first — then the product under the root.
steps: Add the three sides and halve: s = (a+b+c)/2.
Write s−a, s−b, s−c.
Area = √[s(s−a)(s−b)(s−c)]. Take the positive root.
heron.exception: Sides must form a triangle (triangle inequality). s is half the perimeter, not the area. Do not skip the square root.

compound.name: Compound / depreciation / population
compound.phrase: Grow: A = P(1 + r/100)^n. Depreciate: A = P(1 − r/100)^n.
compound.also: Population and compound interest share the growth form.
steps: Write P (start), r% per period, n periods.
Growth / compound / population: multiply by (1 + r/100) each period.
Depreciation / decay: multiply by (1 − r/100) each period.
Raise to n, then multiply by P.
compound.exception: Simple interest is I = Prt/100; simple amount is P + Prt/100 — no power. Compound uses (1±r/100)^n. Depreciation uses minus, not plus. n is the number of compounding periods, not always calendar years if compounded half-yearly.

grouped.name: Grouped mean / median / quartile
grouped.phrase: Mean: Σfm / Σf. Median & quartiles: L + ((N/k − cf)/f)·h.
grouped.also: For median k=2 (N/2); for Q₁ use N/4; for Q₃ use 3N/4.
steps: Find total frequency N = Σf.
Mean: midpoints × frequencies, sum, divide by N.
Median class: first class whose cumulative frequency reaches N/2.
Median = L + ((N/2 − cf)/f)·h. Quartiles swap N/2 for N/4 or 3N/4.
grouped.exception: L is the lower boundary of the median/quartile class; cf is cumulative frequency before that class; f and h belong to that class only. Do not use raw-list median shortcuts on grouped tables.

ages.name: Ages after n years
ages.phrase: After n years, every age gains n. Rewrite the relation with +n on each person.
steps: Let present ages be variables (or use given numbers).
After n years: add n to each age in the story.
Write the equation with the new ages and solve for the present.
ages.exception: "n years ago" subtracts n. Do not add n only to one person. Ratios after n years use (age+n), not age×n.

sets.name: Sets & Venn (SEE)
steps: Sketch two circles; label only A, both, only B, neither.
Both = n(A∩B). Only A = n(A) − both.
Union = only A + both + only B = n(A)+n(B)−both.
Neither = survey total − union.
sets.exception: n(A) already includes the intersection — do not add n(A∩B) again when forming the union. "Only A" is not n(A).

money.name: Currency / commission / VAT
money.phrase: Percent of the stated base. Currency: × rate. Commission/VAT: % of amount.
steps: Name the base: marked price, selling price, or exchange amount.
Currency: multiply or divide by the given rate.
Commission or VAT: amount × rate/100.
Price with VAT: amount × (1 + rate/100).
money.exception: VAT-inclusive reverse uses ÷(1+r/100), not ×(1−r/100). Commission is usually on sales, not on profit unless stated.

menspack.name: Prism / pyramid / packing
menspack.phrase: Prism: V = Bh. Pyramid: V = (1/3)Bh. Packing: total ÷ one unit.
steps: Prism / cuboid: base area × height.
Pyramid / cone idea: one-third of base area × height.
Brick / packing: volume of wall or box ÷ volume of one unit (watch mortar gaps if given).
menspack.exception: Pyramid needs the 1/3 — forgetting it triples the volume. Packing counts whole units; leftover space is not an extra brick unless stated.

probtree.name: Probability trees
probtree.phrase: Multiply along a branch. Add separate paths. Without replacement: the second fraction changes.
steps: Draw the first-stage branches with their probabilities.
From each outcome, draw the next stage (update if without replacement).
A full path: multiply the fractions on that path.
"Or" across paths: add the path probabilities.
probtree.exception: With replacement the second draw stays the same; without replacement the totals drop. Do not add probabilities that sit on the same path.

pythag.name: Pythagoras
pythag.phrase: Legs squared add to hypotenuse squared: a² + b² = c².
steps: Confirm the right angle; c is the side opposite it.
Write a² + b² = c².
Solve for the missing side (root at the end).
pythag.exception: Only right triangles. c must be the longest side. Converse: if a²+b²=c², the angle between a and b is 90°.

bpt.name: Basic proportionality (BPT)
bpt.phrase: A line parallel to one side cuts the other two sides in the same ratio.
steps: Confirm the cut is parallel to the third side.
Write AD/DB = AE/EC (or the full-side form AD/AB = AE/AC).
Cross-multiply and solve.
bpt.exception: Parallel is required — a random transversal does not give equal ratios. Match corresponding segments on each side.

midseg.name: Midsegment theorem
midseg.phrase: Join the midpoints: the midsegment is parallel to the third side and half as long.
steps: Mark midpoints of two sides.
The segment joining them ∥ the third side.
Length = half of that third side.
midseg.exception: Both endpoints must be midpoints. Half the base — not equal to the base.

similar.name: Similarity AAA
similar.phrase: AAA: matching angles → similar triangles → sides in one scale factor.
steps: Show three angles match (two often imply the third).
Write corresponding sides in the same order.
Set up a proportion with one scale factor and solve.
similar.exception: AAA gives similarity, not congruence (SSS/SAS/ASA/RHS). Keep correspondence: largest side faces largest angle.

bisector.name: Angle bisector theorem
bisector.phrase: The bisector cuts the opposite side in the ratio of the adjacent sides.
steps: Confirm the ray bisects the angle.
Write (side)/(side) = (segment)/(segment).
Cross-multiply.
bisector.exception: It splits the opposite side — not the bisector's own length. Ratio uses the two sides that form the angle.

central.name: Center = 2 × rim
central.phrase: Angle at the center is twice the angle at the rim on the same arc.
steps: Identify the shared arc.
Center angle = 2 × rim angle (same arc).
Solve for the unknown.
central.exception: Both angles must stand on the same arc. Rim angle on the major arc is different. Center is at the circle's center, not any interior point.

cyclic.name: Cyclic opposite angles
cyclic.phrase: A quadrilateral is cyclic iff opposite angles sum to 180°.
steps: Spot a cyclic quad (all vertices on a circle).
Opposite angles: A + C = 180°, B + D = 180°.
Solve for the unknown angle.
cyclic.exception: Adjacent angles are not forced to 180° (that would be a trapezoid-with-parallel case). Interior angle ≠ exterior unless stated.

tangent.name: Tangent ⊥ radius
tangent.phrase: A tangent meets the radius at the point of contact at 90°.
steps: Mark the contact point T.
Radius OT ⊥ tangent.
Use right-triangle tools (Pythagoras / trig) in triangle OTP.
tangent.exception: Perpendicular only at the contact point — a line from O to another point on the tangent is not a radius. Two tangents from one point are equal (separate theorem).

altseg.name: Alternate segment
altseg.phrase: Tangent–chord angle equals the angle in the alternate segment.
steps: Find the angle between tangent and chord.
Look to the segment on the other side of the chord.
That rim angle matches.
altseg.exception: "Alternate" means the other segment, not the adjacent one. The tangent must touch at an endpoint of the chord.

eqtang.name: Equal tangents
eqtang.phrase: Two tangents from one outside point are equal in length.
steps: From P, tangents touch at A and B.
PA = PB.
Triangles OAP and OBP are congruent (radii ⊥ tangents).
eqtang.exception: Equal only when both tangents start from the same external point. Chord lengths are a different story.

chord.name: Chord ⊥ from center
chord.phrase: Perpendicular from the center to a chord bisects the chord.
steps: Drop a perpendicular from O to chord AB at M.
M is the midpoint: AM = MB.
In right triangle OMA: r² = d² + (half chord)².
chord.exception: The bisector property needs the perpendicular (or conversely: line from center to midpoint is ⊥). Full chord is twice the half.

exterior.name: Exterior angle
exterior.phrase: Exterior angle of a triangle equals the sum of the two far interior angles.
steps: Extend one side to form the exterior angle.
Exterior = sum of the two remote interiors.
Or: exterior = 180° − adjacent interior.
exterior.exception: Use the two far angles — not the adjacent interior. Polygon exterior sum 360° is a different theorem.

sohcahtoa.name: SOH CAH TOA
sohcahtoa.phrase: SOH CAH TOA: sine opp/hyp, cosine adj/hyp, tangent opp/adj.
steps: Mark the angle; label opposite, adjacent, hypotenuse.
Pick the ratio that uses the sides you know / need.
Solve; keep exact values when the angle is special.
sohcahtoa.exception: Hypotenuse is never opposite or adjacent in the ratio names. Oblique triangles need sine/cosine rules — not plain SOHCAHTOA alone.

astc.name: ASTC signs
astc.phrase: All Sugar Tea Coffee: all → sin → tan → cos positive, going counterclockwise.
steps: Reduce to a reference angle in [0°, 90°].
Find the quadrant of the original angle.
Apply ASTC for the sign; keep the reference value.
astc.exception: ASTC is about signs, not magnitudes. Cot/sec/cosec follow their partners (tan/cos/sin).

hand.name: Special angles hand
hand.phrase: Fist trick: sin = √(fingers before)/2; cos = √(fingers after)/2.
steps: Hold five fingers for 0°, 30°, 45°, 60°, 90°.
Count closed fingers before the angle for sine; after for cosine.
tan = sin/cos; watch 90° (undefined tan).
hand.exception: This builds the acute table only. Other angles need ASTC + reference. tan 90° does not exist.

pyid.name: Pythagorean identity
pyid.phrase: sin²θ + cos²θ = 1. Divide by cos² → 1 + tan²θ = sec²θ.
steps: Start from sin² + cos² = 1.
Given one ratio, isolate the square of the other.
Square root with ±; ASTC picks the sign.
pyid.exception: sin²θ means (sin θ)². sin+cos is not 1. Division by cos² fails where cos = 0.

sinerule.name: Sine rule
sinerule.phrase: a/sin A = b/sin B = c/sin C.
steps: Label side a opposite A, etc.
Use when you know a side and its opposite angle, plus one more.
Cross-multiply; for SSA check the ambiguous case.
sinerule.exception: SSA can give two triangles. SAS / SSS angles need the cosine rule.

cosrule.name: Cosine rule
cosrule.phrase: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A. (Pythagoras with a cosine correction.)
steps: Use for SAS (two sides + included angle) or SSS (three sides → angle).
Side: a² = b² + c² − 2bc cos A, then root.
Angle: cos A = (b² + c² − a²)/(2bc).
cosrule.exception: A must sit between b and c. Obtuse A makes cos negative so a grows. At 90° it collapses to Pythagoras.

compoundang.name: Compound angle sin(A±B)
compoundang.phrase: sin cos cos sin, sign stays: sin(A±B)=sin A cos B ± cos A sin B.
steps: Write sin(A±B) = sin A cos B ± cos A sin B.
Fill each factor; keep exact fractions / surds.
For cos(A±B): cos cos ∓ sin sin (sign swaps).
compoundang.exception: sin(A+B) ≠ sin A + sin B. Cosine flips the middle sign. Check quadrant when expanding numerical angles.

areasine.name: Area ½ab sin C
areasine.phrase: Area = ½ab sin C — half of two sides times the sine of the included angle.
steps: Identify the included angle between the two sides.
Write Area = ½ab sin C.
Use exact sin for special angles.
areasine.exception: C must be the angle between a and b. For a parallelogram drop the ½. Obtuse sin is still positive.
